 Prayer:  This Writ petition has been filed under Article 226 of the  Constitution of India, praying to issue a Writ of Mandamus to direc  second and third respondents to give adequate police protection for  restoration of compound wall in the petitioner's land at Survey No.
 522/2, 522/2A, 522/3B and 542 at Kovalam Panchayat, Kanyakumari  District by considering the respresentation dated 18.02.2023. 
 For Petitioner  : Mr.Isaac Mohanlal, Senior Advocate  for M/s.Isaac Chambers  For Respondents : Mr.A.K.Sriram, Senior Advocate,
 for M/s.S.Ramakrishnan, for R.4 to R.8 an  R.10  : Mr.S.R.Raghunathan,

 ORDER This Writ Petition is filed for issue of Writ of Mandamus directing the second and third respondents to give adequate police protection for restoration of compound wall in the petitioner's land in Survey No.519, 522/2, 522/2A, 522/B and 542 at Kovalam Panchayat, Kanyakumari ____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis District by considering the representation dated 18.02.2023.
2. Subsequent to filing of the Writ Petition, Respondents Nos.4 to 8 were impleaded vide Orders dated 19.04.2023 in WMP.(MD).No . 7929/2023 and Respondents Nos.9 to 11 were impleaded vide Order dated 14.06.2023 in WMP.(MD).No.5240/2023.
3. The facts in brief as per the affidavit and additional affidavit enclosed to this Writ Petition are as under:
The petitioner Trust by name Stella Maris Institute of Development Studies (herein after referred to a the Trust), represented by Executive Director, is a Christian Religious Educational and Charitable Trust registered with registration No.50 of Stella Maris Institute Of Development ... vs The District Collector on 30 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134653242/
2 1997, established by the congregation of daughters of Mary. The Trust was established with the noble object of serving the marginalized population and to extend helping hand to vulnerable children women, senior citizens, children with special needs, terminally sick, people with mental issues and rehabilitation of leprosy people, HIV affected, disabled and Cancer patients, etc., The petitioner Trust has established various institutions to achieve the objectives of the Trust. 
____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 4. The Trust has established rehabilitation centre namely, Stella Maris Leposy and Differently Abled Rehabilitation Centre, at Stella Maris Campus, Sarvodaya Nagar, Kanyakumari District (hereinafter called as the rehabilitation Centre) in the year 1997. It is a non profiteering, non-Governmental,
Charitable Institution managed and administered by the Trust. The rehabilitation centre has been helping about 42 leprosy affective families by providing accommodation, food, medicines,
counselling and self employment training. 
5. The rehabilitation centre is located in the campus of about 2 Acres and 14 cents of land, belonging to Trust, in Survey Nos.519, 522/2, 522/2A, 522/3B and 542 at Kovalam Panchayat, Kanyakumari District. It was purchased in the year 1997 vide Document No.602 of 1997 dated 06.03.1997 registered at Kottaram Sub Registrar Office. Since then, the Trust has been in possession and enjoyment of the property. In the rehabilitation centre, the Trust has constructed 42 houses with private road running across the colony. A compound wall was also constructed surrounding the said land for safety and security of the leprosy affected people. 
___ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ __ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 6. One Mr.Pandian, land broker of that locality has purchased a land adjacent to the rehabilitation centre, with an intention to develop the said land as a layout. The said Pandian has approached one Mr.Alagesan, a politician and both of them have requested the petitioner to permit them to use the approach pathway provided in the Patta land of the rehabilitation centre, as an approach road to the land purchased by the Pandian by demolishing the compound. Despite, there exists another pathway, the said Pandian, intending to have the pathway through the rehabilitation centre. 
Petitioners have rejected the demand of the Pandian and Alagesan stating that the land covered by the rehabilitation centre is a Patta land and meant for the exclusive use of the poor people of rehabilitation centre and in case, if it is made as public pathway, it will affect the rights of poor people in the rehabilitation centre. However the said Pandian started to threatening the persons belonging to petitioner with dire consequences. 
7. On 12.02.2023, at about 11 A.M., Pandian and Alagesan with their henchman, forcefully entered into the rehabilitation centre and demolished the eastern compound wall of the rehabilitation centre and unearthed the gate in the entrance by beating the residents of the centre ____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis who tried to prevent them and in the said incident one Mukesh was severely injured. 
Stella Maris Institute Of Development ... vs The District Collector on 30 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134653242/ 
3 8. The persons belonging to rehabilitation centre have preferred a complaint before the third respondents Kanyakumari Police Station on 12.02.2023 to take suitable action against culprits. They also submitted a representation to the first respondent District Collector on the very same day. The President of the rehabilitation centre also addressed a representation to the District Superintendent of Police on 13.02.2023 about the incident. The petitioner has received a Whatsapp message from Sub Inspector of Police, Kanyakumari Police Station on 17.02.2022, stating that on 12.02.2023 the petitioner complaint was taken on file as C.S.R.No.189/2023 and asked the petitioner to appear for enquiry on 18.02.2023 at about 17.00 hours. After completion of enquiry, the third respondent assured the petitioner that suitable action will be taken. 
9. As the compound wall was demolished for the purpose of safety and security of the families residing in the rehabilitation centre, the petitioner has decided to restore the compound wall with the help of the people from the rehabilitation centre. However, the petitioner was ____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis threatened by Pandian and Alagesan not to restore the compound wall. The petitioner has submitted a representation to the second and third respondents to provide adequate police protection enabling them to restore the compound wall for safety and the interest of poor people. As there was no response this instant Writ Petition is filed. 
10. Counter affidavit has been filed by the respondents Nos.10 and 11 stating that the Writ Petitioner has gifted the subject mentioned property to the beneficiaries under the central government Jawahar Employment Project and that Patta in respect of said land stands in the name of beneficiaries, thereby petitioner is no way concerned with the subject property.
11. It is further mentioned that on 13.05.2015, the Commissioner Agasteeswaram Panchayat Union,
Kanyakumari District has sanctioned concrete road as per proceedings in se.mu.A2/1145/2015-4 dated 13.05.2015, at the place which was shown as street in the sale deeds of the beneficiaries for which a sum of Rs.4,20,000/- was allotted out of the public money and said street is being maintained by Agasteeswaram Panchayat Union, Kanyakumari District as a public pathway, thereby ____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis petitioner can not claim exclusive right over the public pathway. 
12. The petitioner has filed Additional affidavit stating that the petitioner has submitted application to District Surveyor for surveying the land and on 18.04.2023 when the survey was scheduled to be taken up the private respondents of this Writ Petition have raised objection. On 19.04.1993 the petitioner counsel has informed this Court about obstruction made by the private respondents for survey on which this Court directed the concerned revenue officials to conduct the survey and submit the report by 13.06.2023. However on 28.05.2023, the agents of private respondents have trespassed into the lands of rehabilitation centre and parked the JCB.
13. It is further mentioned in the additional affidavit that on 03.06.2023 a notice was received by the petitioner from Tahsildar Agatheeswaam Panchayat Union, Kanyakumari asking the petitioner to be present on 07.06.2023 in VAO office with original documents. On 04.06.2023 at 07.00 P.M.,
Pandian trespassed into the lands of the rehabilitation centre in his vehicle and threatened the people residing in the rehabilitation centre. On 07.06.2023 at 10.30 a.m., Surveyor came to Stella Maris Institute Of Development ... vs The District Collector on 30 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134653242/
4 ____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the land to conduct survey however private respondents created commotion. 
14. Learned counsel for the eleventh respondent has submitted that as per Section 131 of the Tamil Nadu Panchayat Act, 1994 no person shall build any wall, erect any fence, make any encroachment in or over any public road or any property vested to Village Panchayat. It is further submitted that as per Section 236 of the Tamil Nadu Panchayat Act, 1994, all the roads, tanks, wells, waterways vests in and maintained by panchayat shall be opened to the use of enjoyment of all persons. Learned counsel has also filed document to show that electricity connection in respect of street lights stands in the name of the President of Kovalam Panchayat. In the contrary, the petitioner has filed copies bills to show that bills have been paid by the rehabilitation centre. 
15. Learned counsel for the respondents 4 to 8 has filed a copy of a letter dated 13.02.2023 addressed by Commissioner, Agastheeswaram Panchayat Union to the Revenue Divisional Officer stating that Survey No.526/1, 518/5 has been encroached by the petitioner blocking the pathway using the gate. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the ____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis respondent Nos.4 to 8 that field survey was conducted after 13.02.2023 by the Commissioner of Agastheeswaram Panchayat Union, Block Development Officer,
and that according to the survey, concrete road was laid for length of 282 meters at the cost of Rs.4,20,000/- by the panchayat and for the use of public, street lights have also been fixed.
16. On considering the rival contentions and on perusal of records, it is clear that originally the land belonging to Mary Sister Monika, who is the founder of the Trust. Prior to her death Mary Monika has executed a gift deed in favour of Trust as per registered Will on 12.04.2022. The Trust has created rehabilitation centre in Survey No.519,522/2,522/2A, 522/3B and 542 in an extent of 2 acres and 14 cents at Kovalam Panchayat, Kanniyakumari District. Subsequently. permission was obtained for forming layout and for construction of 42 houses vide proceedings No.110 of 2006 t 07 dated 06.07.2006, including for construction of houses internal roads and compound wall. Since then petitioners admittedly have been enjoying the property. As per the layout 42 houses were constructed for 42 families who have been suffering from leprosy and they are residing in the said houses. Permission was also granted for construction of compound wall around the rehabilitation ____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis centre and there is only one entrance towards eastern side. 
17. According to the petitioner, Pandian has purchased the property to the southern side of rehabilitation centre and in order to have access to their land and property which they intend develop, Pandian and his people have highly handedly trespassed into the premises and dismantled southern side compound wall. Eleventh respondent Alagesan is the Chairman of the Panchayat Union. According to him, the roads laid within the rehabilitation centre are vests in the Gram Panchayat and that the Gram Panchayat itself laid their road by spending gram panchayat funds. 
According to him, street lights are erected and electricity was provided by the gram panchayat thereby the petitioner cannot exclusively claim the public road within the rehabilitation centre and it shall be given access to all the villages. 
Stella Maris Institute Of Development ... vs The District Collector on 30 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134653242/ 
5 18 . In the contrary, the submissions of the petitioner is that the road which was laid by the Panchayat is only approach road to the rehabilitation centre and to the said approach road and electric poles were erected and electricity was provided by the Panchayat. It is also submitted that u n o f f i c i a l r e s p o n d e n t s h a v e b e e n c l a i m i n g t h e a c c e s s t o _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the internal roads within the rehabilitation centre which is exclusive property of the rehabilitation centre and that the families living within the rehabilitation centre will have exclusive right over domain over the said land. Learned counsel for the petitioner has also submitted that the roads which are laid internally were gifted by three persons under three different gift deeds and the copies of the same was also filed before this Court. Finally it is submitted that the MRO after surveying the land of the rehabilitation centre as per the directions of this Court has filed a report that the land covered by the road is the Patta land belonging to the petitioner and not the Government Porombokku land. 
19. If at all the roads within the rehabilitation centre were laid by the Gram Panchayat with Gram Panchayat funds and if gram panchayat has got rights on internal road of the rehabilitation centre,
the Gram Panchayat should not have given permission for construction of compound walls encircling entire rehabilitation centre with a gate only on eastern side. In fact there are roads inside the rehabilitation centre which runs from East to West and North to South. If at all Gram Panchayat has got any interest or right over the roads laid inside the rehabilitation centre, the gates should have been opened on western side ____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and northern side, but except eastern side there is no permanent entrance to get into and get out of the rehabilitation centre. Further survey report of the MRO which was conducted as per the directions of this Court also go to show that the land covered by the road, inside the rehabilitation centre is a Patta land and not Government poromboke land. Hence, Panchayat cannot claim any right over it. 
Prima facie it go to show that the entire premises of rehabilitation centre is being exclusively enjoyed by the petitioner and inmates of the rehabilitation centre. 
20. In respect of the compound wall towards southern side is concerned, the photographs show that somebody has dismantled the part of compound wall in order to create entrance. It is not the case of any of the respondents that the petitioner themselves have demolished, the compound wall in the contrary it is the allegation of the petitioners is that Pandian and Alagesan along with their henchmen have trespassed into rehabilitation and demolished the compound wall. 
21. However, the question is whether this Court under 226 of Constitution of India can pass any directions to the respondent police for providing police protection to the petitioner against the unofficial ____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis respondents for giving police protection for re-construction of the compound wall. Though the petitioner has filed this Writ Petition seeking police protection for reconstructing the compound wall, the fact remains is that there is a dispute between the petitioner and un-official respondents in respect of exclusive usage of internal roads of the rehabilitation centre by the petitioner. It is the contention of the petitioner that the roads within the compound wall of the rehabilitation are laid and maintained by the petitioners themselves, whereas Gram Panchayat also claiming that internal roads were laid and being maintained by Gram Panchayat. Similarly, tenth and the eleventh respondents have been claiming access inside the rehabilitation centre for all the people of the village to use the roads inside the Stella Maris Institute Of Development ... vs The District Collector on 30 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134653242/
6 rehabilitation centre.
22. If at all the Gram Panchayat is of the opinion that the petitioner has constructed a compound wall without giving access to the people of the village to use the roads, inside the rehabilitation centre, then the Panchayat Union should have taken steps by filing appropriate suit or by initiating other proceedings for directions to petitioner to dismantle that part of the compound wall so as to give the access to the public to use the internal roads of the rehabilitation centre. However,
____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis according to petitioner the unofficial respondents, Alagesan and Pandian have trespassed and dismantled the part of the compound wall and not the gram panchayat. If at all whatever petitioner has alleged is accepted the unofficial respondents were not expected to take the law into their hands for removal of the compound wall for access inside the rehabilitation centre. 
23. Even otherwise, if at all the compound wall was illegally demolished without following due process either by any of the unofficial respondents or the persons who are not on record, still petitioners cannot seek a relief from this Court, for police protection for re-construction of a compound wall. If at all, there is no dispute from any corner or from any of the parties in this Writ Petition with regard to exclusive use of roads inside the rehabilitation centre and if rights of the petitioner are undisputed then the petitioner can seek direction of the Court to provide suitable police protection. However, there is a serious dispute between the petitioner and other unofficial respondents about of right of petitioner in exclusive use of internal roads of the rehabilitation centre. So the disputed facts between the parties in respect of right of usage of roads cannot be decided by this Court while dealing Writ Petition, under Artice ____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 226 of Constitution of India. 
24. Even if, the tenth and eleventh respondents have illegally dismantled the compound wall and erected a gate, one of the options for the petitioner is to file appropriate Civil Suit seeking appropriate directions including for grant mandatory injunction for construction of a compound wall and may be for perpetual injunction against the respondent not to interfere the activities of the petitioner in the rehabilitation centre. This Court under Article 226 of Constitution of India cannot grant the relief which the petitioner is seeking. 
25. In view of the above, this Writ Petition is dismissed. No costs.
